transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Crestline - Head of ML), Ethan Park (Crestline - Infra Lead), Oliver Grant (Crestline - VP Product)

Summary:
Quarterly check-in to review usage, cost trends, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Discuss Dedicated vs Private/VPC options, SOC2/compliance docs, and specific performance tuning (batching / kv cache / quant profiles). Agree next steps: pricing, security docs, benchmark deep dive, pilot scoping.

Topics:
- Usage & cost trends
- Reliability incidents and mitigation
- Roadmap alignment and upcoming features
- Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
- Action items & next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR for Crestline. Jared from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. With me is Priya, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya: Hi Jared, doing good, thanks. Busy quarter but excited to sync.
[00:16] Ethan: Hey all.
[00:18] Oliver: Hi team.
[00:20] Priya: Thanks for the time. We'll keep this focused on usage, costs, reliability notes and then roadmap alignment.
[00:32] Jared: Quick agenda, usage metrics, incidents, cost optimization opportunities, Dedicated pricing, pilot next steps. Maya, maybe to start can you give us a 30k foot on how things have trended since the last QBR?
[00:44] Maya: Yeah sure. So overall token usage is up about 38% quarter-over-quarter. Our chat sessions are the bulk, around 70% of tokens, embeddings are steady. We're seeing longer sequences on the customer support assistant - average context window went from 1.2k to about 1.9k tokens because of more history retention. Cost has increased accordingly; our bill for Redwood has grown ~42%.
[01:10] Jared: Thanks. That aligns with what we see on our side. Priya, do you want to call out any quick optimization levers?
[01:16] Priya: Yep. A few things: prefix caching/kv caching helps a lot if you can truncate unnecessary history. We also recommended switching to a more aggressive quant profile on some of the lower-sensitivity routes, and enable controlled batching for mid-latency paths. There was a spike where the 95th latency jumped - we think that's from tail queuing during peak traffic.
[01:40] Ethan: Quick question — when you say kv caching is helping, can you show the number? The last email said ~30% CPU savings but could be misunderstood. Also sometimes the transcript shows 'KV cash' ha.
[01:52] Priya: Yeah sorry for the typo in the doc. We meant KV cache. For queries with repeated prefixes caching reduced per-token compute by ~25-35% depending on sequence overlap. If you can push more of the conversation state into the client and use the prefix hash, it saves GPU cycles.
[02:12] Maya: We tried trimming history but saw some user regression in answers. Any guidance on testing?
[02:18] Priya: Start with an A/B where 20% traffic has an aggressive trim policy — evaluate quality metrics on your eval set. We can attach some suggested prompt-preservation heuristics.
[02:30] Oliver: On reliability — we had two incidents last month where latency spiked and a small percentage of requests were retried. Can you walk us through root cause?
[02:39] Jared: Yes, we saw that. Priya — do you want to summarize the incident postmortem?
[02:44] Priya: Sure. On Sept 28th there was a capacity contention on a hosted pool — a batch of long-sequence requests hit a slower kernel path, and the autoscaler had a slight delay scaling up. Two things: one, we had a mis-sized node group for that region; two, some requests routed to a fallback model variant with longer per-token time because of quant profile mismatch. We've adjusted autoscaler thresholds and pinned certain routes to Dedicated-capable pools for you.
[03:10] Ethan: Was that the hosted pool or Dedicated? Because our dedicated reservation should have protected us.
[03:16] Jared: At the time the traffic overflow routed to hosted because Dedicated burst cap was exhausted — we set a higher burst reserve after the incident.
[03:25] Maya: Good to know. Do we have guarantees on tail latency with Dedicated?
[03:29] Priya: Dedicated gives much tighter SLOs because you control the GPU pool; typical 95th latency improvements are 40-60% for similar batch sizes. We can propose a Dedicated config that targets your 95th < 200ms goal.
[03:45] Oliver: Cost wise, Dedicated sounds higher in fixed cost but lower per-token, right? We need a clear run-rate comparison.
[03:50] Jared: Exactly. For sustained throughput Dedicated is almost always more economical. We'll send a side-by-side: hosted per-token vs Dedicated amortized GPU cost with your usage profile. That's part of the pricing sheet we'll send.
[04:05] Maya: Also compliance — the procurement team needs SOC2, ISO docs and a network diagram for Private VPC. Any blockers?
[04:14] Priya: No blockers. We'll attach our SOC2 type II report, ISO27001 cert, and an anonymized network topology for the Private control plane. For Private on-prem, there are extra steps but we've done successful pilots.
[04:28] Ethan: On VPC: latency to our internal services matters. If we go Private, can we still use Redwood Console for trace and cost analytics?
[04:36] Priya: Yes, Console can operate in a Private deployment with connectors. We also support log forwarders to your SIEM. There might be a small additional licensing/ops fee — we'll note that in the doc.
[04:48] Jared: Let's talk roadmap: over the next quarter we'll release a KV cache tuning UI, more granular per-route cost breakdowns, and an optimized kernel path for long sequences on our serving runtime. Priya — timeline?
[04:59] Priya: KV cache UI beta in late Q4, per-route cost drill downs in early Q1. The long-sequence kernel improvements are being upstreamed now; we expect customers to see benefits in Q1 as we ship runtime 2.1.
[05:14] Maya: Will the kernel changes require model re-quant or anything from our side?
[05:18] Priya: Usually not. The runtime picks kernels dynamically, but if you adopt a new quant profile there might be a short validation step. We'll coordinate with Ethan for the validation window.
[05:28] Ethan: For the benchmark deep dive, can we run a sample of our traffic on Redwood Dedicated in our region? We want TTL metrics and real tail distribution.
[05:35] Jared: Yes. We can spin up a short benchmark cluster and replay traffic. We'll need a sanitized sample and expected SLOs. I'll put that as an action item.
[05:46] Oliver: Any discussion with legal on data retention? Our policy is 90 day retention and encryption-at-rest with customer KMS.
[05:54] Priya: We support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated options. Hosted has encrypted-at-rest with rotation, and we can do custom retention rules per contract. We'll include the retention and KMS language in the security pack.
[06:07] Maya: A few asks from our side: 1) cost model with 6/12/24 month Dedicated commit options, 2) SOC2 docs today, 3) a short POC for VPC Private scoped to 2 services, 4) benchmark results.
[06:22] Jared: Great. We'll deliver on those. For the POC, Priya can take the technical lead.
[06:27] Priya: Happy to. Ethan, can you share a sample traffic CSV and a couple representative prompt templates? That helps setup the replay.
[06:36] Ethan: Yes I can. I'll anonymize and share it to the thread by Monday.
[06:40] Jared: Perfect. Any other risks or migration constraints?
[06:44] Maya: Our timeline for next quarter is to decide by end of October whether to move core assistants to Dedicated or keep host + burst. So we're on a tight timeline.
[06:54] Jared: Understood — we'll prioritize pricing and a proposed Dedicated config. We'll also propose a fallback policy to avoid overflow to an incompatible quant profile.
[07:05] Priya: One more note: when you run long sequence batches, watch out for tokenization variance between models; small differences can change billing and latency. We recommend fixing the tokenizer version across your eval harness.
[07:21] Maya: Good point.
[07:24] Jared: Ok recap and next steps. Priya, you'll attach the security pack (SOC2/ISO/network diagram). I'll send pricing and Dedicated amortization by Friday 2026-10-15. We'll schedule the benchmark deep dive for week of 2026-10-19 — Priya and Ethan to coordinate. Maya to confirm success criteria by 2026-10-20.
[07:42] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:45] Oliver: Thanks team.
[07:46] Jared: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with links to the docs and proposed times.
[07:50] End of recording.

Notes: transcript contains occasional ASR errors (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache'), and some speaker attributions may be slightly off. Links referenced: pricing spreadsheet (link shared post-call), SOC2 report (to be attached), benchmark harness README (Priya will share repo link).
